# Orion CLI --help snapshot (COLUMNS=80, ORION_CONFIG unset).
# Regenerate with: python scripts/help_snapshot.py --write

$ orion --help
usage: orion [-h]
             {report,checklist-push,disciplines-push,intake,relay-backfill,install-hook,add-project,graduate-idea,projects,show,check,status,baseline,discussions,bot,relay-serve,relay-user,relay-project}
             ...

Turn local git activity into supervisor-ready progress updates.

positional arguments:
  {report,checklist-push,disciplines-push,intake,relay-backfill,install-hook,add-project,graduate-idea,projects,show,check,status,baseline,discussions,bot,relay-serve,relay-user,relay-project}
    report              Generate and (after preview) send a progress report.
    checklist-push      Push a project's current checklist to the relay (no
                        report); --all for every project, --watch for live
                        updates.
    disciplines-push    Extract a project's disciplines from its docs and push
                        them to the relay (no report).
    intake              Send a pushed/hand-written update for a project (skips
                        collectors & LLM).
    relay-backfill      Push an already-sent report onto the relay dashboard
                        (relay-only, no chat) — for reports sent before the
                        relay was scoped in.
    install-hook        Install a git hook that auto-reports a project on
                        commit/push.
    add-project         Register a new project in orion.toml (the only command
                        that writes config).
    graduate-idea       Register a graduated incubator idea as a new project
                        (delegates to add-project).
    projects            List the projects defined in the config (read-only).
    show                Show one project's resolved config (read-only).
    check               Validate the config and report send-readiness (read-
                        only).
    status              Show which projects have unreported activity across
                        the config (read-only).
    baseline            Mark a project's current state as already-reported
                        WITHOUT sending, so the first real report covers only
                        new activity (skips a giant first report).
    discussions         Read and reply to a project's two-way supervisor
                        discussion thread (E2 Inc 5).
    bot                 Run the Slack bot (PARKED since KI-28 Stage 2; revived
                        with per-user keys).
    relay-serve         Run the local relay: receive pushed reports and serve
                        a read-only dashboard.
    relay-user          Manage relay dashboard users: provision, list, and
                        revoke per-user access keys.
    relay-project       Manage relay project settings: who inside the org may
                        read a project, and whether it is still running or
                        finished.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

$ orion report --help
usage: orion report [-h] [--all] [--config CONFIG] [--yes] [--due] [project]

positional arguments:
  project          Project name as defined in orion.toml (omit when using
                   --all).

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --all            Report on every project in the config (for scheduled --all
                   --yes runs).
  --config CONFIG  Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                   $ORION_CONFIG).
  --yes, -y        Non-interactive: skip the preview for projects with
                   auto_send=true (for unattended/scheduled runs). Projects
                   without auto_send are skipped, never sent. Without --yes,
                   every run previews as usual.
  --due            With --all only: report just the projects DUE under their
                   `cadence` (skip any reported within their interval).
                   Projects with no cadence set are always due. Lets one
                   scheduled `--all --due --yes` serve projects on mixed
                   cadences from a single entry.

$ orion checklist-push --help
usage: orion checklist-push [-h] [--all] [--config CONFIG] [--due] [--watch]
                            [--interval INTERVAL] [--clear-due-soon-days]
                            [--clear-about]
                            [project]

positional arguments:
  project               Project name as defined in orion.toml (omit when using
                        --all; must enable `checklist`).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --all                 Push every checklist-enabled project in the config
                        (for scheduled --all --due runs).
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                        $ORION_CONFIG).
  --due                 With --all only: push just the projects DUE under
                        their `cadence` (skip any pushed within their
                        interval), and skip a due project whose content is
                        unchanged since its last push. Projects with no
                        cadence are always due. Lets one scheduled `--all
                        --due` entry keep every tracker card fresh.
  --watch               Single-project only: run a foreground loop that polls
                        the tasks_file and pushes the checklist whenever it
                        changes, until Ctrl-C (near-real-time edit tracking).
                        Cannot combine with --all/--due.
  --interval INTERVAL   Seconds between polls in --watch mode (default: 3.0).
  --clear-due-soon-days
                        Single-project only: clear this project's stored 'due
                        soon' horizon on the relay, so it falls back to the
                        default. The relay never clears a setting just because
                        a push omits it (KI-35), so dropping `due_soon_days`
                        from config leaves the old horizon in place until you
                        run this.
  --clear-about         Single-project only: clear this project's stored About
                        line on the relay. Like --clear-due-soon-days, the
                        relay never clears About just because a push omits it
                        (KI-35), so removing `about_file` from config leaves
                        the old About in place until you run this.

$ orion disciplines-push --help
usage: orion disciplines-push [-h] [--config CONFIG] [--clear] project

positional arguments:
  project          Project name as defined in orion.toml (must enable the
                   'disciplines' collector).

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG  Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                   $ORION_CONFIG).
  --clear          Retire this project's cards: push an EMPTY set
                   deliberately. A normal push REFUSES to send an empty set
                   (an unreadable doc would otherwise wipe the section
                   silently), so this is the explicit way to clear it. Reads
                   no docs and needs no API key.

$ orion intake --help
usage: orion intake [-h] [--config CONFIG] [--message MESSAGE] [--yes] project

positional arguments:
  project               Project name as defined in orion.toml.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                        $ORION_CONFIG).
  --message MESSAGE, -m MESSAGE
                        The update body. If omitted, the body is read from
                        stdin.
  --yes, -y             Non-interactive: skip the preview and send (for the
                        Claude session skill, which shows the summary for
                        approval in-session first). Redaction still runs;
                        without --yes the preview shows as usual.

$ orion relay-backfill --help
usage: orion relay-backfill [-h] [--config CONFIG] --generated-at GENERATED_AT
                            [--body-file BODY_FILE] [--yes]
                            project

positional arguments:
  project               Project name as defined in orion.toml.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                        $ORION_CONFIG).
  --generated-at GENERATED_AT
                        ISO 8601 timestamp of when the report was ORIGINALLY
                        sent (read it off the delivered Slack/Discord
                        message). Sets the card's time on the dashboard; a
                        naive value is treated as UTC.
  --body-file BODY_FILE
                        Path to a file holding the exact report body. If
                        omitted, the body is read from stdin.
  --yes, -y             Skip the preview/confirm and push (the content was
                        already delivered once). Redaction still runs; without
                        --yes the preview shows as usual.

$ orion install-hook --help
usage: orion install-hook [-h] [--hook {pre-push,post-commit}]
                          [--config CONFIG] [--print] [--force]
                          project

positional arguments:
  project               Project name as defined in orion.toml.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --hook {pre-push,post-commit}
                        Which git hook to install (default: pre-push, which
                        fires when you push — less noisy than post-commit,
                        which fires on every commit).
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                        $ORION_CONFIG).
  --print               Print the hook script to stdout instead of installing
                        it (review first).
  --force               Overwrite an existing hook of the same name.

$ orion add-project --help
usage: orion add-project [-h] [--repo-path REPO_PATH] [--like PROJECT]
                         [--recipient "Name:channel:ENV_VAR"]
                         [--share-level {high_level,detailed}]
                         [--collectors COLLECTORS] [--tasks-file TASKS_FILE]
                         [--notes-file NOTES_FILE]
                         [--tracker-file TRACKER_FILE] [--seed-tasks-from DOC]
                         [--config CONFIG] [--print] [--yes]
                         [--incubator-file INCUBATOR_FILE]
                         [name]

positional arguments:
  name                  Project name (default: the repo directory's name).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo-path REPO_PATH
                        Path to the git repo (default: the current repo's top
                        level, else cwd).
  --like PROJECT        Copy recipients from this existing project (combine
                        with or use instead of --recipient).
  --recipient "Name:channel:ENV_VAR"
                        Add a recipient (repeatable). Channel is "discord" or
                        "slack"; the last field NAMES a .env variable.
  --share-level {high_level,detailed}
                        How much git detail to expose (default: high_level —
                        no code diff).
  --collectors COLLECTORS
                        Comma-separated signals to enable (default: git). Any
                        of: git,tasks,notes,incubator,tracker.
  --tasks-file TASKS_FILE
                        Path to the tasks checklist. If 'tasks' is enabled and
                        this is omitted, defaults to <repo>/TODO.md and
                        creates a starter checklist there.
  --notes-file NOTES_FILE
                        Path to the notes file (required if 'notes' is in
                        --collectors).
  --tracker-file TRACKER_FILE
                        Path to the status-aware tracker doc (required if
                        'tracker' is in --collectors).
  --seed-tasks-from DOC
                        When a tasks_file is being created (no --tasks-file
                        given), seed its checklist from this doc's Markdown
                        tables instead of an empty starter.
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                        $ORION_CONFIG).
  --print               Print the stanza that would be written, and write
                        nothing (review first).
  --yes, -y             Write without the preview confirmation (for non-
                        interactive callers).
  --incubator-file INCUBATOR_FILE
                        Path to the incubator index.md (required if
                        'incubator' is in --collectors).

$ orion graduate-idea --help
usage: orion graduate-idea [-h] [--repo-path REPO_PATH] [--like PROJECT]
                           [--recipient "Name:channel:ENV_VAR"]
                           [--share-level {high_level,detailed}]
                           [--collectors COLLECTORS] [--tasks-file TASKS_FILE]
                           [--notes-file NOTES_FILE]
                           [--tracker-file TRACKER_FILE]
                           [--seed-tasks-from DOC] [--config CONFIG] [--print]
                           [--yes] [--name NAME] [--incubator PROJECT]
                           [--incubator-file INCUBATOR_FILE] [--force]
                           idea

positional arguments:
  idea                  The incubator idea title to graduate (matched case-
                        insensitively).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo-path REPO_PATH
                        Path to the git repo (default: the current repo's top
                        level, else cwd).
  --like PROJECT        Copy recipients from this existing project (combine
                        with or use instead of --recipient).
  --recipient "Name:channel:ENV_VAR"
                        Add a recipient (repeatable). Channel is "discord" or
                        "slack"; the last field NAMES a .env variable.
  --share-level {high_level,detailed}
                        How much git detail to expose (default: high_level —
                        no code diff).
  --collectors COLLECTORS
                        Comma-separated signals to enable (default: git). Any
                        of: git,tasks,notes,incubator,tracker.
  --tasks-file TASKS_FILE
                        Path to the tasks checklist. If 'tasks' is enabled and
                        this is omitted, defaults to <repo>/TODO.md and
                        creates a starter checklist there.
  --notes-file NOTES_FILE
                        Path to the notes file (required if 'notes' is in
                        --collectors).
  --tracker-file TRACKER_FILE
                        Path to the status-aware tracker doc (required if
                        'tracker' is in --collectors).
  --seed-tasks-from DOC
                        When a tasks_file is being created (no --tasks-file
                        given), seed its checklist from this doc's Markdown
                        tables instead of an empty starter.
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                        $ORION_CONFIG).
  --print               Print the stanza that would be written, and write
                        nothing (review first).
  --yes, -y             Write without the preview confirmation (for non-
                        interactive callers).
  --name NAME           Project name (default: a slug derived from the idea
                        title).
  --incubator PROJECT   Which incubator project's index to read (needed only
                        if several exist).
  --incubator-file INCUBATOR_FILE
                        Read the index from this path directly (overrides the
                        config lookup).
  --force               Graduate even if the idea's status is not 'graduated'.

$ orion relay-serve --help
usage: orion relay-serve [-h] [--host HOST] [--port PORT] [--db DB]
                         [--token-env TOKEN_ENV]
                         [--view-token-env VIEW_TOKEN_ENV]
                         [--require-view-auth] [--timezone TIMEZONE]
                         [--session-days SESSION_DAYS] [--allow-legacy-admin]
                         [--disable-legacy-ingest] [--web-dir WEB_DIR]
                         [--showcase] [--showcase-project NAME[:"blurb"]]
                         [--config CONFIG]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --host HOST           Interface to bind (default: 127.0.0.1 — loopback only,
                        not world-reachable).
  --port PORT           Port to bind (default: 8787).
  --db DB               Path to the relay's own sqlite store (default: orion-
                        relay.sqlite3).
  --token-env TOKEN_ENV
                        Name of the .env variable holding the ingest token
                        (default: ORION_RELAY_TOKEN). Must match the token
                        your pushing config's [relay] token_env_var resolves
                        to.
  --view-token-env VIEW_TOKEN_ENV
                        Name of the .env variable holding the dashboard read
                        secret for HTTP Basic auth (default:
                        ORION_RELAY_VIEW_TOKEN). REQUIRED when --host is non-
                        loopback; optional on loopback (reads stay open).
  --require-view-auth   Demand the dashboard view secret even on a loopback
                        bind. Use this when the relay runs on loopback behind
                        a reverse proxy (the proxy exposes it, so 'loopback'
                        isn't actually private) — a forgotten secret then
                        fails closed instead of serving an open dashboard. See
                        docs/deployment.md.
  --timezone TIMEZONE   IANA zone the dashboard renders timestamps in
                        (default: America/Los_Angeles). The relay does not
                        read orion.toml, so this is set here. Examples:
                        --timezone UTC, --timezone "Europe/London". An unknown
                        zone is rejected at startup.
  --session-days SESSION_DAYS
                        Dashboard login session length in days (default: 30).
  --allow-legacy-admin  Keep the legacy shared view key usable as an admin
                        login even after per-user accounts exist (default: off
                        — it is bootstrap-only, usable only while no users
                        have been provisioned).
  --disable-legacy-ingest
                        Retire the shared ingest token on the push path
                        (default: off — the shared token keeps working,
                        anonymously, for backward compatibility). Turn this on
                        once every producer has its own contributor key: the
                        shared token then 401s and only named per-user keys
                        can push. Each legacy use logs a line first, so you
                        can confirm it has gone quiet before flipping this.
  --web-dir WEB_DIR     Path to the built SPA assets (e.g. web/dist) to serve
                        single-host. When set, the relay serves the React
                        dashboard (static assets + an index.html fallback)
                        instead of the legacy server-rendered HTML. Omit to
                        serve the legacy HTML.
  --showcase            Enable the public, no-login Showcase surface (default:
                        off). When on, GET /api/showcase serves ONLY the
                        projects named with --showcase-project; while off it
                        404s and the dashboard hides the Public showcase link.
  --showcase-project NAME[:"blurb"]
                        Add a project to the public Showcase allowlist
                        (repeatable; order is the display order). Optionally
                        append a curated one-line blurb after a colon, e.g.
                        --showcase-project 'orion:A local-first tracker that
                        observes & reframes'. Without a blurb the project's
                        latest report headline is shown. Only effective with
                        --showcase.
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file, used only to locate .env
                        (default: orion.toml; or set $ORION_CONFIG).

$ orion relay-user --help
usage: orion relay-user [-h]
                        {add,list,revoke,grant,ungrant,key,password,role,rename,set-operator,delete}
                        ...

positional arguments:
  {add,list,revoke,grant,ungrant,key,password,role,rename,set-operator,delete}
    add                 Provision a new user and print their one-time access
                        key.
    list                List the relay's users (no credential material is
                        shown).
    revoke              Revoke a user: deactivate their key and force-log-out
                        any live session.
    grant               Grant an existing user access to one or more
                        additional projects.
    ungrant             Remove one or more projects from an existing user's
                        scope (grant's inverse).
    key                 Manage an account's key credentials (add/list/revoke)
                        — replaces `rotate`.
    password            Manage an interactive account's password (set/unlock).
    role                Change an account's role (logs out live sessions; a
                        scoped role needs grants).
    rename              Rename an account (already-recorded history keeps the
                        name it was written with).
    set-operator        Repoint an agent account at a different operating
                        human.
    delete              Hard-delete a user, freeing their name to be reused
                        (revoke keeps the name).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

$ orion relay-user add --help
usage: orion relay-user add [-h]
                            [--role {viewer,admin,supervisor,member,contributor}]
                            [--project PROJECT] [--kind {human,agent}]
                            [--operated-by NAME] [--config CONFIG]
                            name

positional arguments:
  name                  The user's unique display name / handle.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --role {viewer,admin,supervisor,member,contributor}
                        The user's role (default: viewer). An admin sees all
                        projects; a viewer or supervisor is scoped to its
                        granted projects (a supervisor may also post to a
                        project's discussion thread). A contributor is a push-
                        only producer identity: its key authenticates the
                        ingest endpoints for its granted projects but never
                        grants dashboard login. A member is a read-only ORG
                        INSIDER: it sees every org-visible project with no
                        grant at all, plus any grants on top, and can never
                        write anything.
  --project PROJECT     A project this viewer may see (repeatable: --project a
                        --project b). Ignored for an admin's dashboard reads
                        (which see all), but NOT for pushes: every key is
                        scoped to its account's grants. A viewer with none
                        sees nothing.
  --kind {human,agent}  What this account IS (default: human). An 'agent' is a
                        machine identity (Claude Code, a CI job) that pushes
                        on a human's behalf: it must have role contributor and
                        requires --operated-by.
  --operated-by NAME    For --kind agent: the human account this agent acts on
                        behalf of. Its work stays attributed to the agent
                        (badged, 'operated by <name>'), so provenance is never
                        lost.
  --config CONFIG       Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                        $ORION_CONFIG).

positional arguments:

                     keys keep working.
    list             List an account's credentials (never shows the key

    revoke           Revoke ONE credential by id; the account's other keys
                     keep working.

$ orion relay-user password --help
usage: orion relay-user password [-h] {set,unlock} ...

positional arguments:
  {set,unlock}
    set         Set/replace a password (prompts twice, hidden). Their keys

    unlock      Clear a login lockout after failed attempts (does not change

$ orion relay-user password set --help

positional arguments:

options:

  --generate       Have the relay mint a strong password and print it ONCE,

$ orion relay-user password unlock --help
usage: orion relay-user password unlock [-h] [--config CONFIG] name

positional arguments:
  name             The account to unlock.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG  Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                   $ORION_CONFIG).

$ orion relay-user role --help
usage: orion relay-user role [-h] [--config CONFIG] name role

positional arguments:
  name             The account whose role to change.
  role             The new role: admin | viewer | supervisor | member |
                   contributor.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG  Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                   $ORION_CONFIG).

$ orion relay-project --help
usage: orion relay-project [-h] {visibility,lifecycle} ...

positional arguments:
  {visibility,lifecycle}
    visibility          Set whether a project is org-visible or grant-only
                        (restricted).
    lifecycle           Mark a project finished (past) or still running
                        (active).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

$ orion relay-project visibility --help
usage: orion relay-project visibility [-h] [--config CONFIG]
                                      name {org,restricted}

positional arguments:
  name              The project to set.
  {org,restricted}  'org': every member-role account may read it with no per-
                    project grant. 'restricted' (the default for every
                    project): grant-only. Viewers and supervisors are
                    unaffected either way — they always see only their grants.

options:
  -h, --help        show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG   Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                    $ORION_CONFIG).

$ orion relay-project lifecycle --help
usage: orion relay-project lifecycle [-h] [--config CONFIG] name {past,active}

positional arguments:
  name             The project to set.
  {past,active}    'past': the project is finished — it groups into the
                   dashboard's 'Past projects' section and drops out of every
                   deadline view (due-soon, at-risk, slipping, Scheduling), so
                   it can never read as overdue. 'active' (the default every
                   project is born with): the normal live state. Fully
                   reversible.

options:
  -h, --help       show this help message and exit
  --config CONFIG  Path to the config file (default: orion.toml; or set
                   $ORION_CONFIG).
